messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall-sre — realtime latency alert (p95/p99) for production (us-east-1). Threshold breach detected: p95 > 1s for last 5m. Please acknowledge.
Samir K: ack — looking. grabbing dashboards now. which customers impacted?
Marta L: saw a spike on the streaming cluster around 14:03 UTC, p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.1s, p99 to ~8s. no large error surge yet but some streaming stalls reported.
Ryan C: I'm on logs. I see a pattern: many streaming sessions stuck after first chunk, client-side shows connection still open. backend logs show repeated `write timeout` in model-worker.
Jessie P: linking quick graphs: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/streams/latency?var=cluster=us-east-1 — top panel p95/p99, bottom panel active connections.
oncall-sre: taking ownership of triage. runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Streaming+Latency+Runbook
Samir K: quick checks I'll run: 1) confirm infra throttling 2) check model-machine CPU/GPU utilization 3) check recent deploys.
devops-bot: k8s events spike in namespace `redwood-stream-prod` starting 2024-11-03T14:01:22Z: PodEviction and BackOffs observed.
Ryan C: GPUs look healthy on host-level, but I see some pods at 100% memory and kernel oom_killer entries around 14:02:05 in node ip-10-0-7-21.
Jessie P: customer impact: support-bot reports 12 active incidents from customers in East region complaining about stalled streaming and long tail responses. most are degraded UX not full failures.
Samir K: immediate mitigation suggestion: 1) enable fallback routing to replica model variant (cpu-serve) for new sessions, 2) scale up streaming pool +1 replica, 3) temporarily disable long-poll batching. Which is fastest?
Marta L: fastest is fallback routing + spin new pods. I'll trigger route change to route ~20% traffic to stable variant and scale streaming-pool by +2 now.
Marta L: command to scale: ```sh
kubectl -n redwood-stream-prod scale deployment/streaming-worker --replicas=8
```
Marta L: routing change (canary): ```json
POST /internal/routing/v1/canary
{"service":"streaming","route":"stable-variant","percent":20}
```
Samir K: running quick health curl against model worker: `curl -sS http://streaming-worker-1.health/metrics | grep kv_cache_hits` — counts look normal. the timeout traces point at the write path (netty write).
Ryan C: stacking: I can temporarily flip to blocking responses (non-stream) for high-latency sessions to see if streaming path is culprit. need approval?
oncall-sre: do it for canary 5% traffic. prefer minimal customer impact.
Jessie P: support updated customers: "We're aware of streaming stalls in East, engineers are triaging; routing changes in progress." :thumbsup:
devops-bot: scale command accepted, pods spinning up (3 new pods), status: 2/3 ready.
Samir K: checking model inference queue lengths — they spiked same time as stalls. suspect KV-cache thrash after an autoscaler event.
Marta L: I see a recent autoscaler event at 13:59 that terminated a few warm pods, which could explain cache miss spike. adding note to action items.
Ryan C: rolled a small change: disabled continuous-batching on hot-route for 10m: ```yaml
hot-route:
  batching: false
```
Samir K: p95 dropped to ~780ms after the routing canary and extra pods, p99 trending down to 4.3s. still above SLO but improving.
Jessie P: re: customer impact — 3 customers reported timeouts earlier, follow-up sent.
oncall-sre: if p99 doesn't drop under 3s in 10m, escalate to infra pager. set a follow-up timer.
Samir K: log snippet showing write timeout: ```
[14:02:07] WARN netty.WriteTimeoutHandler - write timeout for session id=abcd1234
[14:02:07] ERROR inference.StreamingHandler - failed to send chunk, err=WriteTimeoutException
```
Marta L: handoff plan: I'm patching routing and watching for 15m, then handing to @Ryan C for long-term investigation. @Samir K will follow up on autoscaler tuning and cache warmup.
Ryan C: I've got debug tracing on model-worker and will capture full thread dumps if we see another stall. adding `--trace-kv` for 5m.
Samir K: action items summary: [1] Watch metrics 15m (Marta), [2] Investigate autoscaler termination cause + warmup policy (Samir), [3] Deep-dive on netty write path + thread dumps if recurs (Ryan), [4] Support follow-ups for impacted customers (Jessie).
Jessie P: marking incident as `investigating` in tracker and adding affected customers list. https://redwood.atlassian.net/incident/INC-7892
support-bot: Updated customers notified.
oncall-sre: acknowledged handoff. will re-pager if infra escalates. thanks team :raised_hands:
Samir K: leaving note: next step if regression returns — failover region (us-west) and enable qps-throttling per-customer.
Ryan C: agreed. will prepare runbook snippet for region failover.
Marta L: p95 now ~510ms, p99 ~2.1s, pods stable. I'm handing to Ryan for overnight watch.
Ryan C: taking over. leaving heartbeat every 5m in thread. good job all. :white_check_mark:
